correctness.rationale: The Haagerup/Christensen self-adjoint Schur norm formula is applied to an explicitly constructed PSD order majorant and to permutation-averaged arbitrary majorants. A rank-one factorization proves P-M positive. A two-by-two determinant identity proves P+M positive. For the converse, intersection of two forced intervals for the constant-vector compression produces a scalar inequality, whose exact solution is the claimed bound. All positive integer sizes are covered analytically, with diagnostic rational checks in VERIFY.py.

originality.rationale: The full unequal-part K_{a,b} looped graph family has a sharp exact rational Schur projection norm. Unlike the equal-part case, its permutation group is not transitive, so the Davidson–Donsig/Mathias transitive trace formula is not directly applicable. The previously known singleton-part special case is expressly not counted; the new argument solves the full unequal two-parameter optimization. Relevant literature and available research claims were searched and compared by implication, not only titles. Residual classical graph-multiplier priority risk remains.
residual_risks: The graph-operator-system projection literature could contain a less obvious stronger formula implying the unbalanced case.
An unpublished or unindexed exact matrix-factorization result might cover the two-parameter family.
No independent audit of originality or publication priority has been performed.

value.rationale: The mask for looped complete bipartite graphs is canonical and its exact operator-space Schur projection norm is a natural invariant. The explicit asymmetric two-variable classification identifies sharp limits from fixed one-side size to two-sided growth, distinguishing stars from genuine cycles. This solves an exact invariant across the full natural graph family rather than adding an arbitrary finite sample or numerical improvement.
